items.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...Johnny Lindsay, eh? ... But didn't Jack Paidi play with Johnny? ... You know Johnny Lindsay? [INTERVIEWEE] In my time, I had Bill Beating Drum... Jack Paidi playing trumpet... I forget who was playing bass.

ctx.x: The band be playing back there. That's right. Well, they tore that down and put it out there Homer in Belvin, and call it the Belvin Park. That's where Jack Paidi used to play.

I don't remember, he and his father, and his brother, what is his name? Johnny Lindsay, eh? Good ass. But didn't Jack Paidi play with Johnny? No Johnny Lindsay band? Johnny Lindsay, I don't know. But I know. You know Johnny Lindsay?

In my time, I had Bill Beating Drum, Yank On Trambone. You take, uh... Oh, that boy, he died down there earlier. Julius Granderson playing banjo. I forget who was playing bass. Jack Paidi playing trumpet. Cause his team song, I'll never forget that. Cause I just was getting big enough then. I was around 20 years old then. His team song, If You Don't Like The Way I Do. Yeah. You understand? That was his team song. Cause I was like, you know, I was like, you know. You know what I was like? You know what I was like?…
